podcast.body: In early 1991, during the filming of *Singles*, The Smashing Pumpkins were still a couple of months away from releasing their debut album. Although from Chicago, they would later be "sucked into the whole grunts thing," indicating their eventual association with the broader grunge movement despite their geographical origin. "And the smashing bumpkins, a group that would be sucked into the whole grunts thing even though they were from Chicago, was still a couple of months away from releasing their debut album."

podcast.body: One of the first three albums that established the "defining smashing pumpkin sound" characterized by "big guitars, loud soft dynamics, great drumming, and Billy Corgan's whisper to a wine to his scream vocals." "Those first three albums, Gish, Simea's Dream, and Melon Cully and the Infinite Sadness, found what became the defining smashing pumpkin sound."

podcast.body: Released on May 28, 1991, just three days after the first SoundScan chart, "Gish" was the debut album from The Smashing Pumpkins. Although it was a slow start, the band was among the first to benefit from the new sales tracking data, arriving early to the alternative rock explosion of 1991. "On May 28, 1991, three days after the first ever SoundScan album chart was published, they released their debut album. It was called Yish."

An earlier indie cassette, *Moon*, contained an early version of "Rhinoceros" that "basically served as a demo for Gish." "Before this matching pumpkin signed with the Virgin Records and issued the Gish album in 1991, they released a series of indie cassettes."
